newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - C&W seen as Global One partner.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - C&W seen as Global One partner.

text.p: Cable & Wireless Plc will probably become the British partner of Global One, and could perhaps take a stake in that venture, but would probably be unable to swallow Sprint Corp even if it wanted to.
Analysts said that Global One has no real alternative to C&W if it wants a British partner with a significant market presence, but that going beyond that could be troblesome.
"Given the target market for Global One of multinational companies..there is little choice but Cable and Wireless as a British partner," said analyst Barry Sine of SBC Warburg.

Global One, set up early in 1996, is owned equally by Sprint, Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom. It aims to provide one-stop communications shopping to large corporations and to act as a carrier of international traffic for other telecom companies.

The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday said that C&W had approached France Telecom, which owns 10 percent of Sprint, to get support for a bid for 80 percent of Sprint. The remaining 10 percent is owned by Deutsche Telekom.
France Telecom quickly denied the report, saying that talks had only been about getting C&W as a U.K. partner.
"Cable & Wireless would fit extremely well with Global One," said Guy Woodlief, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Dominant U.K. carrier British Telecommunications Plc is in a rival venture, Concert, with MCI Communications Corp, while National Power Plc's Energis and Telewest Communications Plc would offer less access to businesses than C&W's Mercury unit, Sine said.
C&W, the only large international carrier not in a global alliance, would be in a good position to demand a stake in Global One, rather than in one of its parent companies.
"All of the partners in Global One would be willing to grant equity to a suitable partner to enhance the geogrpahical footprint," said Sine.

Sprint said a bid for it by C&W would be impossible because of a standstill agreement with its European partners, though a spokesman later acknowledged that if all three existing partners agreed it would probably would be possible.

Analysts say C&W's market capitalisation is below what it would have to spend to buy 80 percent of Sprint, and believe bid targets would be unlikely to accept a bid which would include billions of dollars of C&W stock.

C&W's crown jewel is a 57.5 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, which is of uncertain value ahead of the British colony's handover to Chinese rule, though it would also make a tremendous Asian partner for Global One.
"My sense is that the Hong Kong Tel stake is a two-edged sword for Cable and Wireless," said Sine.
Analysts said Sprint already has a coherent and successful U.S. strategy, building on its base in long distance calling.
It is building a Personal Communications Services wireless network called Sprint PCS with three cable TV partners, and is expanding further into local telephone.
From Sprint's perspective they say C&W, which has a relatively small business market operation in the U.S., could do little to enhance that.
